claim: Schistosomes infect more than 200 million of the world's poorest people.
source: Schistosomes infect more than 200 million of the world's poorest people.
evidence: This is a statement of epidemiological fact presented in the abstract, drawing from established scientific knowledge about schistosome infection prevalence.

claim: Schistosomes live in the vasculature.
source: These parasites live in the vasculature, producing eggs that spur a variety of chronic, potentially life-threatening, pathologies exacerbated by the long lifespan of schistosomes, that can thrive in the host for decades.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the anatomical location of schistosome parasites in their mammalian hosts.

claim: Schistosomes produce eggs that spur chronic, potentially life-threatening pathologies.
source: These parasites live in the vasculature, producing eggs that spur a variety of chronic, potentially life-threatening, pathologies exacerbated by the long lifespan of schistosomes, that can thrive in the host for decades.
evidence: This is established knowledge about schistosome pathogenesis.

claim: Schistosomes can thrive in the host for decades.
source: These parasites live in the vasculature, producing eggs that spur a variety of chronic, potentially life-threatening, pathologies exacerbated by the long lifespan of schistosomes, that can thrive in the host for decades.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the longevity of schistosome infections.

claim: Somatic stem cells in Schistosoma mansoni are biased towards generating a population of cells expressing factors associated with the schistosome host-parasite interface.
source: Here, we demonstrate that somatic stem cells in Schistosoma mansoni are biased towards generating a population of cells expressing factors associated exclusively with the schistosome host-parasite interface, a structure called the tegument.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by transcriptional profiling and EdU pulse-chase experiments shown in the figures.

claim: Cells expressing tegumental factors are short-lived and rapidly turned over.
source: We show cells expressing these tegumental factors are short-lived and rapidly turned over.
evidence: This is supported by EdU pulse-chase experiments showing rapid labeling and subsequent loss of EdU+ tsp-2+ cells (Figure 3).

claim: Stem cell-driven renewal of the tegumental lineage represents an important strategy for parasite survival in the context of the host vasculature.
source: We suggest that stem cell-driven renewal of this tegumental lineage represents an important strategy for parasite survival in the context of the host vasculature.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data presented in the study.

claim: Neoblasts are pluripotent stem cells essential for regeneration and tissue homeostasis in free-living flatworms.
source: Neoblasts are pluripotent stem cells essential for regeneration and tissue homeostasis in a variety of free-living flatworms, most notably freshwater planarians (Newmark and Sánchez Alvarado, 2002; Wagner et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature on planarian neoblasts.

claim: Schistosomes possess neoblasts capable of self-renewal and differentiation into tissues such as the intestine and muscle.
source: Previously, it was shown that schistosomes, like their free-living relatives, also possess neoblasts, capable of self-renewal and differentiation into tissues such as the intestine and muscle (Collins et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: 135 genes were down-regulated in both irradiation and RNAi datasets.
source: From our transcriptional profiling experiments of male somatic tissues we identified 135 genes that were down regulated (≥1.25x, p<0.05) in both our irradiation and RNAi datasets (Figure 1b, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by transcriptional profiling data shown in Figure 1b and Supplementary file 1.

claim: The 135 down-regulated genes include known stem cell-specific genes such as nanos2 and ago2-1.
source: As anticipated, this gene set included a number of known stem cell- (e.g., nanos2 and ago2-1[Collins et al., 2013]) and cell cycle-specific (cyclinB and mcm2) genes (Figure 1b,c and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 1b,c and Supplementary file 1, with citation to previous work identifying these as stem cell markers.

claim: 105 genes were not down-regulated at D2 post-irradiation but were significantly down-regulated at D14 post-irradiation and following RNAi of fgfrA or histone H2B.
source: More importantly, we identified 105 genes that were not down-regulated at D2 post-irradiation but were significantly down regulated (≥1.25x, p<0.05) at D14 post-irradiation and following RNAi of either fgfrA or histone H2B (Figure 1b,c and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by transcriptional profiling data shown in Figure 1b,c and Supplementary file 1.

claim: The schistosome orthologue of p53 was down-regulated approximately 2-fold at 48 hr and nearly 150-fold at D14 post-irradiation.
source: The most striking example of this class was the schistosome orthologue of the planarian p53 (Pearson and Sánchez Alvarado, 2010), which was down-regulated ~2 fold at 48 hr and nearly 150 fold at D14 post-irradiation (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by data in Supplementary file 1 and citation to previous work on planarian p53.

claim: Expression of cathepsin B was unaffected at D2 and D7 following irradiation.
source: As anticipated, expression of cathepsin B, a gene expressed in differentiated intestinal cells, was unaffected at either time point (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Expression of neoblast-associated genes fgfrA and nanos2 was substantially reduced at D2 and did not return by D7 following irradiation.
source: Conversely, the expression of genes associated with the neoblasts (fgfrA and nanos2) was substantially reduced at D2 and the expression of these genes did not return by D7 (Figure 2a), confirming that stem cells are irreversibly depleted by irradiation.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Irradiation irreversibly depletes stem cells in schistosomes.
source: Conversely, the expression of genes associated with the neoblasts (fgfrA and nanos2) was substantially reduced at D2 and the expression of these genes did not return by D7 (Figure 2a), confirming that stem cells are irreversibly depleted by irradiation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that neoblast marker expression does not recover after irradiation, as shown in Figure 2a.

claim: The number of cells expressing p53 is modestly reduced at D2 post-irradiation and dramatically reduced by D7.
source: Consistent with our RNAseq data, the number of cells expressing p53 is modestly reduced at D2 post-irradiation and dramatically reduced by D7 (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: At D2 post-irradiation, the number of cells expressing DIS genes tsp-2, sm13, sm29, and val-8 was unaffected.
source: In contrast to the neoblast-expressed genes and p53, at D2 the number of cells expressing the DIS genes tsp-2, sm13, sm29, and val-8 was unaffected (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: By D7 post-irradiation, the expression of DIS genes tsp-2, sm13, sm29, and val-8 was severely depleted.
source: However, by D7 post-irradiation the expression of these genes was severely depleted (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: There is no co-expression of the DIS gene tsp-2 with histone H2B.
source: We observed no co-expression of the DIS gene tsp-2 with histone H2B Figure 2—figure supplement 1, suggesting that DIS genes are expressed in a population of cells other than neoblasts.
evidence: This is supported by double FISH data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: DIS genes are expressed in a population of cells other than neoblasts.
source: We observed no co-expression of the DIS gene tsp-2 with histone H2B Figure 2—figure supplement 1, suggesting that DIS genes are expressed in a population of cells other than neoblasts.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of co-expression between tsp-2 and histone H2B shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: p53 is expressed in both histone H2B+ neoblasts and tsp-2+ cells.
source: Consistent with our observations following irradiation, we observed that p53 was expressed in both the histone H2B+ neoblasts and tsp-2+ cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by double FISH data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: DIS genes are expressed in an irradiation-sensitive population of cells that is molecularly distinct from neoblasts.
source: Together, these data strongly support the model that the DIS genes are expressed in an irradiation-sensitive population of cells that is molecularly distinct from the neoblasts.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined observations of delayed loss of DIS gene expression after irradiation and lack of co-expression with neoblast markers.

claim: A number of DIS genes encode proteins previously shown to be associated with the parasite's surface.
source: Upon closer examination we noted that a number of the DIS genes encoded proteins previously shown by immunological and/or proteomic approaches to be associated with the parasite's surface (e.g., tsp-2 (Tran et al., 2006; Pearson et al., 2012; Wilson, 2012), sm13 (Abath et al., 2000; Wilson, 2012), sm29 (Braschi and Wilson, 2006; Cardoso et al., 2008; Wilson, 2012), sm25 (Abath et al., 1999; Castro-Borges et al., 2011; Wilson, 2012)).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous immunological and proteomic studies.

claim: The schistosome surface is covered by a continuous syncytial structure called the tegument.
source: The schistosome surface is covered by a continuous syncytial structure, called the tegument (Figure 2b), which serves as the primary barrier between the parasite and its host.
evidence: This is established knowledge about schistosome anatomy, illustrated in Figure 2b.

claim: The tegument serves as the primary barrier between the parasite and its host.
source: The schistosome surface is covered by a continuous syncytial structure, called the tegument (Figure 2b), which serves as the primary barrier between the parasite and its host.
evidence: This is established knowledge about tegument function.

claim: The tegument is connected by cytoplasmic bridges to nucleated cell bodies that sit in the mesenchyme beneath the parasite's body-wall muscles.
source: This unique tissue is connected by cytoplasmic bridges to nucleated cell bodies that sit in the mesenchyme, beneath the parasite's body-wall muscles (Morris and Threadgold, 1968; Wilson and Barnes, 1974) (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous ultrastructural studies and illustrated in Figure 2b.

claim: A majority of tsp-2+ cells are located immediately beneath the parasite's body-wall muscle layer.
source: Consistent with tsp-2 being expressed in a tegument-associated cell population, we found that a majority of tsp-2+ cells are located immediately beneath the parasite's body-wall muscle layer (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is supported by FISH data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: TSP-2 is a well-characterized tegument-specific factor.
source: We first examined the distribution of the mRNA for a Tetraspanin, TSP-2, that encodes a well-characterized tegument-specific factor (Braschi and Wilson, 2006; Tran et al., 2006; Pearson et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies characterizing TSP-2.

claim: TSP-2 is currently being explored as an anti-schistosome vaccine candidate due to its presence on the parasite surface.
source: TSP-2 is currently being explored as an anti-schistosome vaccine candidate due to its presence on the parasite surface (Hotez et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work on vaccine development.

claim: DIS genes encoding known tegumental factors are expressed in a largely overlapping population of cells with tsp-2 immediately beneath the dorsal body-wall muscles.
source: We observed that DIS genes encoding a panel of known tegumental factors, including sm13 (Smp_195190), sm29 (Smp_072190), sm25 (Smp_195180), an amino acid transporter (Smp_176940) (Wilson, 2012), a dysferlin protein (Smp_141010) (Braschi and Wilson, 2006; Wilson, 2012), an endophillin B1 (Castro-Borges et al., 2011; Wilson, 2012), and a cd59-like molecule (Smp_081920) (Wilson, 2012) were expressed in a largely overlapping population of cells with tsp-2 immediately beneath the dorsal body-wall muscles (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is supported by double FISH data shown in Figure 2c and citations to previous work identifying these as tegumental factors.

claim: tsp-2+ cells represent a population of tegument-associated cells.
source: Given their position in the parasite, and their expression of many known tegumental genes, our data indicate that tsp-2+ cells represent a population of tegument-associated cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the anatomical position of tsp-2+ cells and their co-expression of known tegumental factors.

claim: At D1 following an EdU pulse, less than 0.25% of tsp-2+ cells were EdU+.
source: At D1 following an EdU pulse, <0.25% of tsp-2+ cells were EdU+ (Figure 3b,c), indicating that the tsp-2+ cells are not proliferative.
evidence: This is supported by EdU pulse-chase data shown in Figure 3b,c.

claim: tsp-2+ cells are not proliferative.
source: At D1 following an EdU pulse, <0.25% of tsp-2+ cells were EdU+ (Figure 3b,c), indicating that the tsp-2+ cells are not proliferative.
evidence: This is inferred from the very low percentage of EdU+ tsp-2+ cells at D1, shown in Figure 3b,c.

claim: After a 3-day chase period, over 40% of tsp-2+ cells were newly born EdU+ cells.
source: After a 3-day chase period, however, we noted that over 40% of tsp-2+cells were newly born EdU+ cells (Figure 3b,c).
evidence: This is supported by EdU pulse-chase data shown in Figure 3b,c.

claim: Stem cells initially incorporating EdU are capable of replenishing nearly half of the tsp-2+ cells within three days.
source: This result suggests that stem cells initially incorporating EdU were capable of replenishing nearly half of the tsp-2+ cells within three days.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that over 40% of tsp-2+ cells become EdU+ by D3.

claim: Beyond D5, there was a rapid reduction in the number of tsp-2+ EdU+ cells and an overall reduction in EdU levels per cell.
source: Beyond D5, we noted a rapid reduction in the number of tsp-2+ EdU+ cells and an overall reduction in the EdU levels per cell (Figure 3b,c).
evidence: This is supported by EdU pulse-chase data shown in Figure 3b,c.

claim: tsp-2+ cells are a short-lived cell population that is continuously renewed by neoblasts during the parasite's life in its definitive host.
source: These data suggest that tsp-2+ cells are a short-lived cell population that is continuously renewed by the neoblasts during the parasite's life in its definitive host.
evidence: This is inferred from the rapid labeling and subsequent loss of EdU+ tsp-2+ cells shown in Figure 3.

claim: Only 2.5% of cathepsin B+ intestinal cells were EdU+ at D3, and this level remained fairly constant throughout the 11D time course.
source: In contrast to the tsp-2+ cells, only 2.5% of cathespin B+ intestinal cells were EdU+ at D3, and this level remained fairly constant throughout the 11D time course (Figure 3b,d).
evidence: This is supported by EdU pulse-chase data shown in Figure 3b,d.

claim: The kinetics of tegumental cell birth differs from that of intestinal cells.
source: Thus, the kinetics of tegumental cell birth differs from that of intestinal cells.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the EdU labeling kinetics of tsp-2+ cells versus cathepsin B+ cells shown in Figure 3.

claim: On a population level, neoblasts are 'biased' toward the rejuvenation of tsp-2+ cells over other lineages.
source: Taken together, our data suggest that on a population level neoblasts are 'biased' toward the rejuvenation of tsp-2+ cells over other lineages.
evidence: This is inferred from the much higher rate of EdU incorporation into tsp-2+ cells compared to intestinal cells.

claim: In planarians, a population of postmitotic neoblast progeny displays similar sensitivity to irradiation as the tsp-2+ tegument-associated cell population in schistosomes.
source: In planarians, a population of postmitotic neoblast progeny displays similar sensitivity to irradiation as this tsp-2+ tegument-associated cell population (Eisenhoffer et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work on planarian neoblast progeny.

claim: Planarian neoblast progeny express a p53-like protein and a large collection of planarian-specific molecules.
source: These planarian neoblast progeny similarly express a p53-like protein as well as a large collection of planarian-specific molecules (Eisenhoffer et al., 2008; Zhu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work on planarian neoblast progeny.

claim: Planarian neoblast progeny serve as progenitors to terminally differentiated epidermal cells.
source: Most importantly, these planarian cells serve as progenitors to terminally differentiated epidermal cells (van Wolfswinkel et al., 2014; Tu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work on planarian epidermal differentiation.

claim: Free-living and parasitic flatworms utilize similar developmental strategies for epidermal maintenance.
source: Thus, it appears that free-living and parasitic flatworms utilize similar developmental strategies for epidermal maintenance.
evidence: This is inferred from the similarities between planarian neoblast progeny and schistosome tsp-2+ cells.

claim: Electron microscopy is the only methodology to unambiguously identify tegumental cell bodies in schistosomes.
source: Presently, electron microscopy is the only methodology to unambiguously identify tegumental cell bodies in schistosomes.
evidence: This is a statement about current technical limitations in the field.

claim: A primary function of schistosome neoblasts is to generate cells that contribute to the tegument.
source: Regardless of which model (or combination of these models) is correct, our data suggest that a primary function of the schistosome neoblasts is to generate cells that contribute to the tegument.
evidence: This is inferred from the high rate of neoblast differentiation into tsp-2+ cells shown in the EdU pulse-chase experiments.

claim: The tegument is important in defending the parasite from host immunity.
source: In the case of schistosomes, there is little dispute about the importance of the tegument in defending the parasite from host immunity (McLaren, 1980; Skelly and Alan Wilson, 2006), yet the properties of this tissue that afford the parasite protection in blood are unclear.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work on tegument function.

claim: The properties of the tegument that afford the parasite protection in blood are unclear.
source: In the case of schistosomes, there is little dispute about the importance of the tegument in defending the parasite from host immunity (McLaren, 1980; Skelly and Alan Wilson, 2006), yet the properties of this tissue that afford the parasite protection in blood are unclear.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Neoblast-driven tegumental regeneration may play a key role in the parasite's ability to survive in the mammalian host.
source: Based on our data, we suggest that neoblast-driven tegumental regeneration may play a key role in the parasite's ability to survive in the mammalian host.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data presented in the study.

claim: By undergoing continuous tegumental renewal, the parasite is likely capable of rapidly turning over the tegument and regenerating damage inflicted inside the host.
source: By undergoing continuous tegumental renewal, the parasite is likely capable of rapidly turning over the tegument and regenerating damage inflicted inside the host (e.g., via immune attack).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the functional significance of the observed tegumental cell turnover.

claim: Expression of genes in differentiated tissues is unaffected at 48 hr following irradiation, whereas neoblasts are irreversibly killed.
source: To examine the transcriptional effects of neoblast ablation, we exploited the observation that expression of genes in differentiated tissues (e.g., the intestine) is unaffected at 48 hr following irradiation, whereas the neoblasts are irreversibly killed (Collins et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Many genes down-regulated at 48 hr following irradiation are associated with schistosome neoblasts.
source: Previously, we demonstrated that many genes down-regulated at 48 hr following irradiation were associated with the schistosome neoblasts (Collins et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Genes down-regulated at both early and late time points after neoblast ablation are expected to be neoblast-enriched factors.
source: Specifically, we expected genes down-regulated at both early and late time points to be neoblast-enriched factors, whereas genes only down-regulated at later time points would be genes that require neoblasts for maintaining their expression.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the interpretation of the experimental design.

claim: Genes only down-regulated at later time points after neoblast ablation are genes that require neoblasts for maintaining their expression.
source: Specifically, we expected genes down-regulated at both early and late time points to be neoblast-enriched factors, whereas genes only down-regulated at later time points would be genes that require neoblasts for maintaining their expression.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the interpretation of the experimental design.

claim: Parasites treated with histone H2B dsRNA display a rapid and robust loss of neoblasts.
source: Parasites treated with histone H2B dsRNA display a rapid and robust loss of neoblasts. n > 5 parasites. Scale bar: 200 µm.
evidence: This is supported by EdU labeling data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: val-8 mRNA levels show a modest increase 48 hr post-irradiation.
source: We did note in our RNAseq experiments, and in independent qPCR experiments, a modest increase in val-8 mRNA levels 48 hr post-irradiation (Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by RNAseq data in Figure 1 and qPCR data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The number of val-8+ cells did not dramatically change at 48 hr post-irradiation.
source: Since, the number of val-8+ cells did not appear to dramatically change at 48 hr post-irradiation (Figure 2a), it is possible that some val-8+ cells had elevated levels of the val-8 mRNA.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Some val-8+ cells may have elevated levels of val-8 mRNA at 48 hr post-irradiation.
source: Since, the number of val-8+ cells did not appear to dramatically change at 48 hr post-irradiation (Figure 2a), it is possible that some val-8+ cells had elevated levels of the val-8 mRNA.
evidence: This is speculated to explain the discrepancy between increased mRNA levels and unchanged cell numbers.

claim: Adult S. mansoni (6–8 weeks post-infection) were obtained from infected mice by hepatic portal vein perfusion.
source: Adult S. mansoni (6–8 weeks post-infection) were obtained from infected mice by hepatic portal vein perfusion with 37°C DMEM (Mediatech, Manassas, VA) plus 5% Fetal Bovine Serum (FBS, Hyclone/Thermo Scientific Logan, UT) and heparin (200–350 U/ml).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: Parasites were exposed to 200 Gy of γ-irradiation using a Gammacell-220 Excel with a Co60 source for transcriptional profiling experiments.
source: For transcriptional profiling of irradiated worms, parasites were harvested from mice, suspended in Basch medium 169, and exposed to 200 Gy of γ-irradiation using a Gammacell-220 Excel with a Co60 source (Nordion, Ottawa, ON, Canada).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: Three independent biological replicates were performed for both control and irradiated experimental groups in transcriptional profiling experiments.
source: Three independent biological replicates were performed for both control and irradiated experimental groups.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: Three biological replicates were performed for fgfrA(RNAi) and two biological replicates for H2B(RNAi).
source: Three biological replicates were performed for fgfrA(RNAi) and two biological replicates for H2B(RNAi).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: RNAseq analysis was performed on an Illumina HiSeq2000.
source: To measure transcriptional differences, RNAseq analysis was performed on an Illumina HiSeq2000 and analyzed using CLC Genomics Workbench as described previously (Collins et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used in the study.
This is quantitative data from EdU pulse-chase experiments shown in Figure 3b.
This is quantitative data from EdU pulse-chase experiments shown in Figure 3b.

claim: Some cells expressing lower levels of tsp-2 are located more internally, but a majority of tsp-2+ cells are located just beneath the parasite muscle layer.
source: Although some cells expressing lower levels of tsp-2 are located more internally, a majority of tsp-2+ cells were located just beneath the parasite muscle layer.
evidence: This is an observation from FISH data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Neoblasts and tsp-2+ cells are distinct cell populations.
source: tsp-2 is not expressed in histone H2B+ stem cells, whereas p53 is expressed in the histone H2B+ cells. tsp-2 and p53 are co-expressed. Thus, neoblasts and tsp-2+cells are distinct and both express p53.
evidence: This is inferred from the double FISH data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both neoblasts and tsp-2+ cells express p53.
source: tsp-2 is not expressed in histone H2B+ stem cells, whereas p53 is expressed in the histone H2B+ cells. tsp-2 and p53 are co-expressed. Thus, neoblasts and tsp-2+cells are distinct and both express p53.
evidence: This is supported by double FISH data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.
